title.zh: 卷三十八 志第十八: 地理一
title.raw: 卷三十八 志第十八: 地理一 Volume 38 Treatises 18: Geography 1

meta.sourceNote: Body replaced from Wikisource raw text after ChineseNotes scrape due to glyph/encoding artifacts.

sentences.zh: 志第二十二職官一=【序】=高祖發跡太原，官名稱位，皆依隋舊。

translations.literal: Treatise 22: Offices and Ranks 1 = [Preface] = When the High Ancestor rose from Taiyuan, official titles and ranks all followed the Sui precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Treatise 22, Offices and Ranks, Part 1 — Preface. When Emperor Gaozu first rose in Taiyuan, the names and ranks of offices all followed Sui practice.

sentences.zh: 及登極之初，未遑改作，隨時署置，務從省便。

translations.literal: When he first ascended the throne, he had no leisure to reform them; offices were appointed as occasion required, striving for economy and convenience.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of his reign he had not yet had time to redesign the system; posts were filled as needed, with every effort toward simplicity and convenience.

sentences.zh: 武德七年定令：以太尉、司徒、司空為三公。

translations.literal: The statutes fixed in the seventh year of Wude: taking Grand Preceptor, Minister of Education, and Minister of Works as the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: The code promulgated in the seventh year of Wude (624) defined the Three Dukes as the Grand Preceptor, the Minister of Education, and the Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 尚書、門下、中書、秘書、殿中、內侍為六省。

translations.literal: Department of State Affairs, Chancellery, Secretariat, Secretariat Archive, Palace Administration, and Palace Domestic Service — as the Six Departments.
translations.idiomatic: The Six Departments were the Department of State Affairs, the Chancellery, the Secretariat, the Archive Secretariat, the Palace Administration, and the Palace Domestic Service.

sentences.zh: 次御史台；

translations.literal: Next, the Censorate;
translations.idiomatic: Next came the Censorate;

sentences.zh: 次太常、光祿、衛尉、宗正、太僕、大理、鴻臚、司農、太府，為九寺；

translations.literal: Next, Director of Ceremonies, Director of Banquets, Director of the Guard, Director of the Imperial Clan, Director of the Stud, Director of Justice, Director of Guests, Director of Agriculture, and Director of the Treasury — as the Nine Directorates;
translations.idiomatic: then the nine directorates: Ceremonies, Banquets, the Guard, the Imperial Clan, the Stud, Justice, Guests, Agriculture, and the Treasury;

sentences.zh: 次將作監；

translations.literal: Next, the Directorate of Works;
translations.idiomatic: then the Directorate of Works;

sentences.zh: 次國子學；

translations.literal: Next, the National University;
translations.idiomatic: then the National University;

sentences.zh: 次天策上將府；

translations.literal: Next, the Heavenly Stratagem General-in-Chief Office;
translations.idiomatic: then the Heavenly Stratagem General-in-Chief Office;

sentences.zh: 次左右衛、左右驍衛、左右領軍、左右武候、左右監門、左右屯、左右領，為十四衛府。

translations.literal: Next, Left and Right Guards, Left and Right Valiant Cavalry, Left and Right Army Inspectors, Left and Right Military Inspectors, Left and Right Gatekeepers, Left and Right Garrisons, and Left and Right Commanders — as the Fourteen Guard Offices.
translations.idiomatic: then the fourteen guard offices: the Left and Right Guards, Valiant Cavalry, Army Inspectors, Military Inspectors, Gatekeepers, Garrisons, and Commanders.

sentences.zh: 東宮置三師、三少、詹事府、門下典書兩坊。

translations.literal: The Eastern Palace had Three Preceptors, Three Junior Preceptors, the Household Administration of the Heir Apparent, and the two bureaus of the Chancellery Archive.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Palace was staffed with the Three Preceptors, the Three Junior Preceptors, the Household Administration of the Heir Apparent, and the two bureaus of the Chancellery and Archive.

sentences.zh: 次內坊；

translations.literal: Next, the Inner Bureaus;
translations.idiomatic: Then the inner bureaus;

sentences.zh: 次家令、率更、僕三寺；

translations.literal: Next, the three directorates of the Household Steward, the Timekeeper, and the Servants;
translations.idiomatic: then the three palace directorates: the Household Steward, the Timekeeper, and the Servants;

sentences.zh: 次左右衛率府、左右宗衛率府、左右虞候率府、左右監門率府、左右內率府，為十率府。

translations.literal: Next, Left and Right Guard Commandant Offices, Left and Right Imperial Clan Guard Commandant Offices, Left and Right Patrol Commandant Offices, Left and Right Gate Commandant Offices, and Left and Right Inner Commandant Offices — as the Ten Commandant Offices.
translations.idiomatic: then the ten commandant offices of the heir's guard, imperial clan guard, patrol guard, gate guard, and inner guard, left and right.

sentences.zh: 王公以下置府佐國官。

translations.literal: For princes and dukes downward, mansion aides and fief officials were established.
translations.idiomatic: Princes and dukes and below were assigned mansion aides and fief officials.

sentences.zh: 公主置邑司已下。

translations.literal: For princesses, fief administrations and subordinate offices were established.
translations.idiomatic: Princesses were provided with fief administrations and subordinate staff.

sentences.zh: 並為京職事官。

translations.literal: All were capital duty-holding officials.
translations.idiomatic: All of these were capital offices with substantive duties.

sentences.zh: 州縣、鎮戍、岳瀆、關津為外職事官。

translations.literal: Prefectures and counties, garrison commands, sacred mountains and rivers, and passes and fords — as external duty-holding officials.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectures and counties, frontier garrisons, offices for sacred mountains and rivers, and passes and fords were external duty-holding offices.

sentences.zh: 又以開府儀同三司從一品、特進正二品、左光祿大夫從二品、右光祿大夫正三品、散騎常侍從三品、太中大夫正四品、通直散騎常侍正四品、中大夫從四品上、員外散騎常侍從四品下、中散大夫正五品上、散騎侍郎正五品下、通直散騎侍郎從五品上、員外散騎侍郎從五品下、朝議郎、承議郎正六品、通議郎、通直郎從六品、朝請郎、宣德郎正七品、朝散郎、宣義郎從七品、給事郎、征事郎正八品、承奉郎、承務郎從八品、儒林郎、登仕郎正九品、文林郎、將仕郎從九品，並為文散官。

translations.literal: Also, Honored Companion with Ceremony Equal to the Three Dukes, junior first rank; Extraordinary Promoter, senior second rank; Left Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, junior second rank; Right Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, senior third rank; Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, junior third rank; Grand Master of Palace Counsel, senior fourth rank; Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry for Direct Communication, senior fourth rank; Master of Palace Counsel, junior fourth rank, upper grade; Extra Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, junior fourth rank, lower grade; Master of Scattered Counsel, senior fifth rank, upper grade; Gentleman of the Scattered Cavalry, senior fifth rank, lower grade; Regular Gentleman of the Scattered Cavalry, junior fifth rank, upper grade; Extra Gentleman of the Scattered Cavalry, junior fifth rank, lower grade; Court Consultant and Gentleman for Supporting Discussion, senior sixth rank; Master of Discussion and Master for Direct Discussion, junior sixth rank; Gentleman Invited to Court and Gentleman for Proclaiming Virtue, senior seventh rank; Gentleman for Court Service and Gentleman for Proclaiming Righteousness, junior seventh rank; Gentleman Attendant and Gentleman for Campaign Affairs, senior eighth rank; Gentleman for Receiving Service and Gentleman for Receiving Duties, junior eighth rank; Gentleman of the Forest of Learning and Gentleman for Entering Office, senior ninth rank; Gentleman of Literary Elegance and Gentleman Awaiting Office, junior ninth rank — all civil honorary ranks.
translations.idiomatic: The civil honorary ranks were Honored Companion with Ceremony Equal to the Three Dukes at junior first rank; Extraordinary Promoter at senior second rank; the Left Grand Master for Splendid Happiness at junior second rank; the Right Grand Master for Splendid Happiness at senior third rank; Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry at junior third rank; and the full sequence of masters, gentlemen, and candidate ranks from Grand Master of Palace Counsel through Gentleman Awaiting Office at junior ninth rank.

sentences.zh: 輔國正二品、鎮軍從二品二大將軍，冠軍正三品、雲麾從三品、忠武、壯武、宣威、明威、信遠、遊騎、遊擊自正四品上到從五品下十將軍，為散號將軍，以加武士之無職事者。

translations.literal: Auxiliary-to-the-State at senior second rank and Pacifier of the Army at junior second rank as the two great generals; Champion at senior third rank and Cloud Banner at junior third rank; Loyal Martial, Robust Martial, Proclaimer of Might, Bright Might, Trustworthy Far-reaching, Roaming Cavalry, and Roaming Strike from senior fourth rank, upper grade through junior fifth rank, lower grade as the ten generals — prestige-title generals used to honor warriors without substantive posts.
translations.idiomatic: The two great generals Auxiliary-to-the-State and Pacifier of the Army ranked senior and junior second rank; Champion and Cloud Banner ranked senior and junior third rank; and the ten prestige generals from Loyal Martial through Roaming Strike, ranging from senior fourth rank, upper grade to junior fifth rank, lower grade, served as honorary military titles for men of arms who held no substantive office.

sentences.zh: 改上開府儀同三司為上輕車都尉，開府儀同三司為輕車都尉，儀同三司為騎都尉，秦王、齊王下統軍為護軍，副統軍為副護軍，上大都督為驍騎尉，大都督為飛騎尉，帥都督為雲騎尉，都督為武騎尉，車騎將軍為游騎將軍，親衛驃騎將軍為親衛中郎將，其勳衛驃騎准此。

translations.literal: Superior Open-the-Feudal-Office Equal in Ceremony with the Three Dukes was changed to Superior Commandant of Light Chariots; Open-the-Feudal-Office Equal in Ceremony with the Three Dukes to Commandant of Light Chariots; Equal in Ceremony with the Three Dukes to Commandant of Cavalry; army commander under the Prince of Qin and Prince of Qi to Protector of the Army; deputy army commander to deputy Protector of the Army; superior great commander to Commandant of Valiant Cavalry; great commander to Commandant of Flying Cavalry; leading commander to Commandant of Cloud Cavalry; commander to Commandant of Martial Cavalry; Chariot-and-Cavalry General to Roaming Cavalry General; Personal Guard Swift-Cavalry General to Personal Guard Central Commander — with the Merit Guard Swift-Cavalry by the same rule.
translations.idiomatic: Superior Open-the-Feudal-Office was renamed Superior Commandant of Light Chariots; the ordinary and lesser grades of that title became Commandants of Light Chariots and Cavalry; army commanders under the Princes of Qin and Qi became Protectors of the Army, with deputies as deputy protectors; command ranks were renamed commandants of valiant, flying, cloud, and martial cavalry; the Chariot-and-Cavalry General became Roaming Cavalry General; and the Personal and Merit Guard Swift-Cavalry Generals became central commanders of the guard.

sentences.zh: 親衛車騎將軍為親衛郎將，其勳衛翊衛車騎並准此。

translations.literal: Personal Guard Chariot-and-Cavalry General became Personal Guard Commandant — with Merit Guard and Wing Guard chariot-and-cavalry by the same rule.
translations.idiomatic: The Personal Guard Chariot-and-Cavalry General became Personal Guard Commandant, and the Merit and Wing Guards followed the same pattern.

sentences.zh: 監門府郎將為監門中郎將，領左右郎將，准此。

translations.literal: Gate Office commandant became Gate Office central commander; leading left and right commandants — by the same rule.
translations.idiomatic: The Gate Office commandant became Gate Office central commander, and the leading left and right commandants were treated likewise.

sentences.zh: 諸軍驃騎將軍為統軍，其秦王、齊王下領三衛及庫直、驅咥直、車騎並准此。

translations.literal: Swift-Cavalry Generals of the various armies became army commanders; those under the Prince of Qin and Prince of Qi leading the Three Guards, as well as armory duty, drive duty, and chariot-and-cavalry — by the same rule.
translations.idiomatic: Swift-Cavalry Generals in the field armies became army commanders, and the same applied to officers under the Princes of Qin and Qi who led the Three Guards, armory duty, drive duty, and chariot-and-cavalry units.

sentences.zh: 諸軍車騎將軍為別將。

translations.literal: Chariot-and-Cavalry Generals of the various armies became separate commanders.
translations.idiomatic: Chariot-and-Cavalry Generals in the various armies were renamed separate commanders.

sentences.zh: 其散官文騎尉為承議郎，屯騎尉為通直郎，雲騎尉為登仕郎，羽騎尉為將仕郎。

translations.literal: Among prestige offices: Literary Cavalry Commandant became Supporter of Proposals; Garrison Cavalry Commandant became Regular Communication Gentleman; Cloud Cavalry Commandant became Entering Office Gentleman; Feathered Cavalry Commandant became Candidate for Office Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Among the prestige ranks, Literary Cavalry Commandant became Supporter of Proposals, Garrison Cavalry Commandant became Regular Communication Gentleman, Cloud Cavalry Commandant became Entering Office Gentleman, and Feathered Cavalry Commandant became Candidate for Office Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 武德九年，罷天策上將府。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Wude, the Heavenly Stratagem General-in-Chief Office was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Wude (626), the Heavenly Stratagem General-in-Chief Office was abolished.

sentences.zh: 貞觀元年，改國子學為國子監，分將作為少府監，通將作為三監。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenguan, the National University was changed to the Directorate of the Sons of the State; Works was split into the Directorate of the Palace Workshops, and Works in general became the Three Directorates.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhenguan (627), the National University became the Directorate of the Sons of the State; the Works directorate was divided into the Palace Workshops Directorate, and together they formed the three directorates.

sentences.zh: 八年七月，始以雲麾將軍為從三品階。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the eighth year, the Cloud Banner General was first made a secondary third-rank grade.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the eighth year (634), the Cloud Banner General was first assigned to the secondary third rank.

sentences.zh: 九月，以統軍正四品下，別將正五品上。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, army commander was made primary fourth rank, lower grade; separate commander, primary fifth rank, upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, the army commander was set at primary fourth rank, lower grade, and the separate commander at primary fifth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 十一年，改令置太師、太傅、太保為三師。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, the code was revised to establish Grand Preceptor, Grand Tutor, and Grand Protector as the Three Preceptors.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year (637), the code was revised to establish the Grand Preceptor, Grand Tutor, and Grand Protector as the Three Preceptors.

sentences.zh: 其三公已下，六省、一台、九寺、三監、十二衛、東宮諸司，並從舊定。

translations.literal: From the Three Dukes downward, the Six Departments, one Censorate, Nine Directorates, Three Directorates, Twelve Guards, and Eastern Palace offices — all followed the former fixations.
translations.idiomatic: From the Three Dukes downward, the Six Departments, Censorate, nine directorates, three supervisory directorates, twelve guards, and Eastern Palace offices all remained as previously defined.

sentences.zh: 又改以光祿大夫為從二品，金紫光祿大夫為正三品，銀青光祿大夫為從三品，正議大夫為正四品上，通議大夫為正四品下，太中大夫為從四品上，中大夫為從四品下，中散大夫為正五品上，朝議大夫為正五品下，朝請大夫為從五品上，朝散大夫為從五品下。

translations.literal: Also changed: Master of Splendid Happiness to secondary second rank; Master of Splendid Happiness with Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon to primary third rank; Master of Splendid Happiness with Silver Seal and Blue Ribbon to secondary third rank; and so through Regular Counsel Master, Communication Counsel Master, Grand Palace Counsel Master, Palace Counsel Master, Scattered Counsel Master, Court Discussion Master, Court Invitation Master, and Court Disbursement Master to their respective grades.
translations.idiomatic: The prestige ranks were also reassigned: Master of Splendid Happiness to secondary second rank; the gold-seal and silver-seal masters of splendid happiness to primary and secondary third rank; and the masters of regular counsel, communication counsel, grand palace counsel, palace counsel, scattered counsel, court discussion, court invitation, and court disbursement to their respective fourth- and fifth-rank grades.

sentences.zh: 其六品下，唯改通議郎為奉議郎，自餘依舊。

translations.literal: For sixth rank and below, only Communication Discussion Gentleman was changed to Offering Discussion Gentleman; the rest followed the old.
translations.idiomatic: For the sixth rank and below, only Communication Discussion Gentleman was renamed Offering Discussion Gentleman; all other titles remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 更置驃騎大將軍為從一品武散官；

translations.literal: Swift-Cavalry Grand General was newly established as a secondary first-rank military prestige office;
translations.idiomatic: The Swift-Cavalry Grand General was newly created as a secondary first-rank military prestige office;

sentences.zh: 輔國、鎮軍二大將軍為從二品武散官。

translations.literal: Assistant-to-the-State and Pacifier-of-the-Army, the two great generals, as secondary second-rank military prestige offices.
translations.idiomatic: while Assistant-to-the-State and Pacifier-of-the-Army became secondary second-rank military prestige offices.

sentences.zh: 冠軍將軍加大字。

translations.literal: Champion General had the character "grand" added.
translations.idiomatic: The title Champion General was enlarged to Grand Champion General.

sentences.zh: 及雲麾已下、遊擊已上，改為五品已上武散官。

translations.literal: From Cloud Banner downward and Roaming Strike upward, they were changed to military prestige offices of fifth rank and above.
translations.idiomatic: From Cloud Banner down through Roaming Strike up, these became military prestige offices of the fifth rank and above.

sentences.zh: 又置昭武、振威、致果、翊麾、宣節、禦武、仁勇、陪戎八校尉副尉自正六品至從九品，上階為校尉，下為副尉。

translations.literal: Also established were eight commandants and deputy commandants — Illustrious Martial, Quelling Might, Achieving Fruit, Assisting Banner, Proclaiming Festival, Defending Martial, Humane Courage, and Escorting Arms — from senior sixth rank to junior ninth rank; the upper grades were commandants, the lower deputy commandants.
translations.idiomatic: Eight pairs of commandants and deputy commandants were also created — Illustrious Martial, Quelling Might, Achieving Fruit, Assisting Banner, Proclaiming Festival, Defending Martial, Humane Courage, and Escorting Arms — ranging from senior sixth rank to junior ninth rank, with the higher grades styled commandants and the lower deputy commandants.

sentences.zh: 為六品已下武散官。

translations.literal: These were military honorary ranks below the sixth rank.
translations.idiomatic: These served as military honorary ranks below the sixth rank.

sentences.zh: 凡九品已上職事，皆帶散位，謂之本品。

translations.literal: For all substantive offices of ninth rank and above, prestige rank was always carried — called the basic rank.
translations.idiomatic: Every substantive office from the ninth rank upward carried a prestige rank, which was called one's basic rank.

sentences.zh: 職事則隨才錄用，或從閑入劇，或去高就卑，遷從出入，參差不定。

translations.literal: Substantive posts were assigned according to talent; one might move from light duty to heavy, or leave high for low — transfers in and out were irregular and not fixed.
translations.idiomatic: Substantive appointments followed talent: one might move from a light post to a demanding one, or step down from high to low office, with transfers in every direction and no fixed pattern.

sentences.zh: 散位則一切以門廕結品，然後勞考進敘。

translations.literal: Prestige rank was in all cases first fixed by hereditary privilege, and only afterward advanced by merit review.
translations.idiomatic: Prestige rank, by contrast, was first established entirely through hereditary privilege, and only later advanced by merit review.

sentences.zh: 《武德令》，職事高者解散官，欠一階不到為「兼」。

translations.literal: In the Wude Code, when the substantive post was higher, the prestige office was set aside; if one grade short and not equal, it was called "concurrent."
translations.idiomatic: Under the Wude Code, if the substantive post outranked the prestige title, the prestige title was set aside; if the appointee fell one grade short of the post, the designation was "concurrent."

sentences.zh: 職事卑者，不解散官。

translations.literal: When the substantive post was lower, the prestige office was not set aside.
translations.idiomatic: When the substantive post was lower than the prestige rank, the prestige title was retained.

sentences.zh: 《貞觀令》，以職事高者為「守」，職事卑者為「行」，仍各帶散位。

translations.literal: In the Zhenguan Code, when the substantive post was higher it was called "acting"; when lower, "performing" — in each case still carrying prestige rank.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhenguan Code called a higher substantive appointment "acting" and a lower one "performing," while in both cases the holder still bore his prestige rank.

sentences.zh: 其欠一階，依舊為「兼」，與當階者，皆解散官。

translations.literal: If one grade short, it was still "concurrent" as before; if equal in grade, prestige office was set aside in all cases.
translations.idiomatic: If the appointee was one grade short, the old label "concurrent" still applied; if he matched the grade of the post, the prestige title was set aside.

sentences.zh: 永徽已來，欠一階者，或為兼，或帶散官，或為守，參而用之。

translations.literal: From Yonghui onward, when one grade short, sometimes concurrent, sometimes carrying prestige office, sometimes acting — applied in mixed fashion.
translations.idiomatic: From the Yonghui era onward, when an appointee was one grade short, "concurrent," retention of the prestige title, or "acting" were applied in varying combinations.

sentences.zh: 其兩職事者亦為「兼」，頗相錯亂。

translations.literal: Those with two substantive posts were also called "concurrent," which was quite confused.
translations.idiomatic: Holders of two substantive posts were also labeled "concurrent," which led to considerable confusion.

sentences.zh: 其欠一階之「兼」，古念反。

translations.literal: The "acting concurrently" for one grade short is read gù-niàn.
translations.idiomatic: The character for "acting concurrently" when one grade short is read gù-niàn.

sentences.zh: 其職事之兼，古恬反。

translations.literal: The "acting concurrently" for two executive offices is read gù-tián.
translations.idiomatic: The character for "acting concurrently" when holding two executive posts is read gù-tián.

sentences.zh: 字同音異耳。

translations.literal: The character is the same; only the pronunciation differs.
translations.idiomatic: The written character is the same; only the pronunciation differs.

sentences.zh: 咸亨二年，始一切為「守」。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianheng, everything was first uniformly made "acting."
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xianheng (671), the designation was uniformly standardized as "acting."

sentences.zh: 自高宗之後，官名品秩，屢有改易。

translations.literal: After Emperor Gaozong, office names and grades were repeatedly changed.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Gaozong, office titles and ranks were changed again and again.

sentences.zh: 今錄永泰二年官品。

translations.literal: Now recorded are the office grades of the second year of Yongtai.
translations.idiomatic: What follows records the official grades as of the second year of Yongtai (766).

sentences.zh: 其改易品秩者，注於官品之下。

translations.literal: Those whose grades were changed are noted below the office grades.
translations.idiomatic: Changes in grade are noted beneath each entry in the grade table.

sentences.zh: 若改官名及職員有加減者，則各附之於本職云。

translations.literal: If office names were changed or staff numbers increased or decreased, each is appended to its substantive post.
translations.idiomatic: Changes in office names or in the number of incumbents are recorded separately under each substantive office.

sentences.zh: 唐初因隋號，武德三年三月，改納言為侍中，內史令為中書令，給事郎為給事中，內書省為中書省。

translations.literal: Early Tang followed Sui designations; in the third month of the third year of Wude, Supplicator was changed to Palace Attendant, Inner Scribe Director to Secretariat Director, Gentleman of Service to Attendant of Affairs, and Inner Scribe Department to Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Early Tang initially kept Sui titles; in the third month of the third year of Wude (620), Supplicator became Palace Attendant, Inner Scribe Director became Secretariat Director, Gentleman of Service became Attendant of Affairs, and the Inner Scribe Department became the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 貞觀二十三年六月，改民部尚書為戶部尚書。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the twenty-third year of Zhenguan, Minister of the People was changed to Minister of the Household.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the twenty-third year of Zhenguan (649), the Minister of the People was renamed Minister of the Household.

sentences.zh: 七月，改治書侍御史為御史中丞，改諸州治中為司馬，別駕為長史，治禮郎為奉禮郎。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, Drafting Attendant Censor was changed to Censor-in-Chief; in all prefectures, Administrator was changed to Administrative Aide, Vice Director to Chief Aide, and Ritual Gentleman to Offering Ritual Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month, the Drafting Attendant Censor became Censor-in-Chief; in all prefectures the administrator became administrative aide, the vice director became chief aide, and the ritual gentleman became offering ritual gentleman.

sentences.zh: 顯慶元年，改戶部尚書為度支尚書，侍郎為度支侍郎。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianqing, Minister of the Household was changed to Minister of Revenue, Vice Minister to Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xianqing (656), the Minister of the Household was renamed Minister of Revenue, and the vice minister likewise.

sentences.zh: 又置驃騎大將軍員，從一品。

translations.literal: Also established a Swift-Cavalry Grand General post, secondary first rank.
translations.idiomatic: A post of Swift-Cavalry Grand General was also created at the secondary first rank.

sentences.zh: 龍朔二年二月甲子，改百司及官名。

translations.literal: On the first day of the second month of the second year of Longshuo, the hundred offices and their names were changed.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiazi day of the second month of the second year of Longshuo (662), the names of the hundred offices were all changed.

sentences.zh: 改尚書省為中台，僕射為匡政，左右丞為肅機，左右司郎中為丞務，吏部為司列，主爵為司封，考功為司績，禮部為司禮，祠部為司禋，膳部為司膳，主客為司蕃，戶部為司元，度支為司度，倉部為司倉，金部為司珍，兵部為司戎，職方為司域，駕部為司輿，庫部為司庫，刑部為司刑，都官為司僕，比部為司計，工部為司平，屯田為司田，虞部為司虞，水部為司川，余司依舊。

translations.literal: Department of State Affairs to Central Terrace; Vice Directors to Rectifiers of Governance; Left and Right Assistants to Custodians of the Secretariat; Left and Right Bureau Directors to Assistants in Affairs; Ministry of Personnel to Bureau of Rosters; etc., through the remaining bureaus — other offices followed the old.
translations.idiomatic: The Department of State Affairs became the Central Terrace; vice directors became Rectifiers of Governance; assistants became Custodians of the Secretariat; bureau directors became Assistants in Affairs; Personnel became Bureau of Rosters; Fiefs became Bureau of Enfeoffments; Merit Review became Bureau of Records; Rites became Bureau of Rites; Sacrifices became Bureau of Sacrifices; Provisions became Bureau of Provisions; Guests became Bureau of Foreign Guests; Household became Bureau of Origins; Revenue became Bureau of Measures; Granaries became Bureau of Granaries; Coinage became Bureau of Treasures; War became Bureau of Arms; Appointments became Bureau of Territories; Transport became Bureau of Carriages; Stores became Bureau of Stores; Punishments became Bureau of Punishments; Justice became Bureau of Retainers; Audit became Bureau of Accounts; Works became Bureau of Equilibrium; Colonies became Bureau of Fields; Forestry became Bureau of Parks; Waterways became Bureau of Rivers; the remaining offices kept their old names.

sentences.zh: 尚書為太常伯，侍郎為少常伯，郎中為大夫。

translations.literal: Ministers became Grand Regular Preceptors; Vice Ministers, Junior Regular Preceptors; Directors, Grand Masters.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers were titled Grand Regular Preceptors, vice ministers Junior Regular Preceptors, and directors Grandees.

sentences.zh: 中書門下為東西台。

translations.literal: Secretariat and Chancellery became Eastern and Western Terraces.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat and Chancellery became the Eastern and Western Terraces.

sentences.zh: 侍中為左相，黃門侍郎為東台侍郎，給事中為東台舍人，散騎常侍為左右侍極，諫議大夫為正諫大夫。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant became Left Chancellor; Yellow Gate Vice Minister, Eastern Terrace Vice Minister; Attendant of Affairs, Eastern Terrace Draftsman; Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, Left and Right Attendants-in-Waiting; Remonstrance Master, Regular Remonstrance Master.
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Attendant became Left Chancellor; the Yellow Gate Vice Minister became Eastern Terrace Vice Minister; the Attendant of Affairs became Eastern Terrace Draftsman; the Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry became Left and Right Attendants-in-Waiting; and the Remonstrance Master became Regular Remonstrance Master.

sentences.zh: 中書令為右相，侍郎為西台侍郎，舍人為西台舍人。

translations.literal: Secretariat Director became Right Chancellor; Vice Minister, Western Terrace Vice Minister; Draftsman, Western Terrace Draftsman.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat Director became Right Chancellor; the vice minister became Western Terrace Vice Minister; and the draftsman became Western Terrace Draftsman.

sentences.zh: 秘書省為蘭台，監為太史，少監為侍郎，丞為大夫。

translations.literal: Archive Secretariat became Orchid Terrace; Director, Grand Astrologer; Vice Director, Vice Minister; Assistant, Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: The Archive Secretariat became the Orchid Terrace; its director became Grand Astrologer, the vice director Vice Minister, and the assistant Grand Master.

sentences.zh: 著作郎為司文郎中，太史令為秘閣郎中。

translations.literal: Compilation Gentleman became Bureau of Writings Director; Grand Astrologer Director, Secret Pavilion Director.
translations.idiomatic: The Compilation Gentleman became Director of the Bureau of Writings; the Grand Astrologer became Director of the Secret Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 御史台為憲台，御史大夫為大司憲，御史中丞為司憲大夫。

translations.literal: Censorate became Law Terrace; Censor-in-Chief, Grand Law Administrator; Attendant Censor-in-Chief, Law Administrator Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: The Censorate became the Law Terrace; the Censor-in-Chief became Grand Law Administrator; and the Attendant Censor-in-Chief became Law Administrator Grand Master.

sentences.zh: 殿中省為中禦府，丞為大夫。

translations.literal: Palace Administration became Central Imperial Household; Assistant, Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Administration became the Central Imperial Household, and its assistant became Grand Master.

sentences.zh: 尚食為奉膳，尚藥為奉醫，尚衣為奉冕，尚舍為奉扆，尚乘為奉駕，尚輦為奉禦，並為大夫。

translations.literal: Director of Food became Offering Food; Director of Medicine, Offering Medicine; Director of Robes, Offering Crowns; Director of Lodgings, Offering Screens; Director of Transport, Offering Carriages; Director of Palanquins, Offering Imperial Service — all as Grand Masters.
translations.idiomatic: The directors of food, medicine, robes, lodgings, transport, and palanquins became Offerings of Food, Medicine, Crowns, Screens, Carriages, and Imperial Service, each titled Grand Master.

sentences.zh: 內侍省為內侍監。

translations.literal: Palace Domestic Service became Palace Domestic Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Domestic Service became the Palace Domestic Directorate.

sentences.zh: 太常為奉常，光祿為司宰，衛尉為司衛，宗正為司宗，太僕為司馭，大理為詳刑，正為大夫。

translations.literal: Director of Ceremonies became Offering Regular; Director of Banquets, Bureau of Sacrifices; Director of the Guard, Bureau of Guard; Director of the Imperial Clan, Bureau of the Clan; Director of the Stud, Bureau of Carriage; Director of Justice, Detailed Punishments — directors as Grand Masters.
translations.idiomatic: Ceremonies became Offering Regular; Banquets became Bureau of Sacrifices; the Guard became Bureau of Guard; the Imperial Clan became Bureau of the Clan; the Stud became Bureau of Carriage; Justice became Detailed Punishments; and each director was titled Grand Master.

sentences.zh: 鴻臚為司文，司農為司稼，太府為外府，卿並為正卿。

translations.literal: Director of Guests became Bureau of Writings; Director of Agriculture, Bureau of Harvests; Director of the Treasury, Outer Treasury — all directors as Regular Directors.
translations.idiomatic: Guests became Bureau of Writings; Agriculture became Bureau of Harvests; the Treasury became Outer Treasury; and all directors were titled Regular Director.

sentences.zh: 少府監為內府監。

translations.literal: Palace Workshops Directorate became Inner Treasury Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Workshops Directorate became the Inner Treasury Directorate.

sentences.zh: 將作監為繕工監，大匠為大監，少匠為少監。

translations.literal: Works Directorate became Repair Works Directorate; Chief Artisan, Grand Director; Junior Artisan, Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: The Works Directorate became the Repair Works Directorate; the chief artisan became Grand Director and the junior artisan Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 國子監為司成館，國子祭酒為大司成，司業為少司成，博士為宣業。

translations.literal: Directorate of the Sons of the State became Academy of Accomplishment; Rector, Grand Accomplisher; Vice Rector, Junior Accomplisher; Erudite, Proclaimer of Accomplishment.
translations.idiomatic: The Directorate of the Sons of the State became the Academy of Accomplishment; the rector became Grand Accomplisher, the vice rector Junior Accomplisher, and the erudite Proclaimer of Accomplishment.

sentences.zh: 都水為司津監。

translations.literal: Director of Waterways became Directorate of Fords.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of Waterways became the Directorate of Fords.

sentences.zh: 左、右衛府、左、右驍衛府、左、右武衛府，並除「府」字。

translations.literal: Left and Right Guard Offices, Left and Right Valiant Cavalry Offices, Left and Right Martial Guard Offices — all had the character "office" removed.
translations.idiomatic: The Left and Right Guards, Valiant Cavalry, and Martial Guards all dropped the word "office" from their titles.

sentences.zh: 左、右屯衛府為左右威衛，左、右領軍衛為左右戎衛，武候為金吾衛，千牛為奉宸衛，屯營為羽林軍。

translations.literal: Left and Right Garrison Guard Offices became Left and Right Majestic Guards; Left and Right Army Inspector Guards became Left and Right Military Guards; Military Inspector became Golden Crow Guard; Thousand-Ox became Offering Imperial Guard; Garrison Camp became Feathered Forest Army.
translations.idiomatic: The Left and Right Garrison Guards became Left and Right Majestic Guards; the Army Inspector Guards became Military Guards; the Military Inspectors became Golden Crow Guards; the Thousand-Ox Guards became Offering Imperial Guards; and the Garrison Camp became the Feathered Forest Army.

sentences.zh: 詹事為端尹府，門下、典書為左右春坊，左右庶子為左右中護。

translations.literal: Household Administrator became Rectifier-in-Chief Office; Chancellery and Archive became Left and Right Spring Bureaus; Left and Right Junior Preceptors became Left and Right Central Protectors.
translations.idiomatic: The Household Administrator became the Rectifier-in-Chief Office; the Chancellery and Archive became the Left and Right Spring Bureaus; and the left and right junior preceptors became Left and Right Central Protectors.

sentences.zh: 中允為左贊善大夫，洗馬為司經大夫，中舍人為右贊善大夫。

translations.literal: Central Approver became Left Assistant-in-Goodness Grand Master; Groom, Classics Grand Master; Central Draftsman, Right Assistant-in-Goodness Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: The Central Approver became Left Assistant-in-Goodness Grand Master; the Groom became Classics Grand Master; and the Central Draftsman became Right Assistant-in-Goodness Grand Master.

sentences.zh: 家令寺為宮府寺，率更寺為司更寺，僕寺為馭僕寺，長官並為大夫。

translations.literal: Household Steward Directorate became Palace Household Directorate; Timekeeper Directorate, Bureau of Time Directorate; Servants Directorate, Driving Servants Directorate — all chiefs as Grand Masters.
translations.idiomatic: The Household Steward Directorate became the Palace Household Directorate; the Timekeeper became the Bureau of Time; the Servants became the Driving Servants Directorate; and each chief was titled Grand Master.

sentences.zh: 左、右衛率府為典戎衛，左、右宗衛率府為司禦衛，左右虞候率府為清道衛，監門率府為崇掖衛，內率府為奉裕衛。

translations.literal: Left and Right Guard Commandant Offices became Model Military Guards; Left and Right Imperial Clan Guard Commandant Offices, Bureau of Imperial Guards; Left and Right Patrol Commandant Offices, Clear-the-Way Guards; Gate Commandant Office, Honored Flank Guards; Inner Commandant Office, Offering Abundance Guards.
translations.idiomatic: The Left and Right Guard Commandants became Model Military Guards; the Imperial Clan Commandants became Bureau of Imperial Guards; the Patrol Commandants became Clear-the-Way Guards; the Gate Commandant became Honored Flank Guard; and the Inner Commandant became Offering Abundance Guard.

sentences.zh: 七日，又制廢尚書令，改起居郎為左史，起居舍人為右史，著作佐郎為司文郎，太史丞為秘閣郎，左右千牛為奉宸，司議郎為左司議郎，太子舍人為右司議郎。

translations.literal: On the seventh day, it was also ordered to abolish Director of the Department of State Affairs; Court Diary Gentleman to Left Scribe; Court Diary Draftsman to Right Scribe; Compilation Assistant to Bureau of Writings Gentleman; Grand Astrologer Assistant to Secret Pavilion Gentleman; Left and Right Thousand-Ox to Offering Imperial; Discussion Gentleman to Left Discussion Gentleman; Heir Apparent Draftsman to Right Discussion Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: On the seventh day it was further ordered to abolish the Director of the Department of State Affairs; the Court Diary Gentleman became Left Scribe and the draftsman Right Scribe; the compilation assistant became Bureau of Writings Gentleman and the astrologer assistant Secret Pavilion Gentleman; the left and right Thousand-Ox became Offering Imperial; the Discussion Gentleman became Left Discussion Gentleman and the heir's draftsman Right Discussion Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 典膳、藥藏、內直監、宮門大夫，並改為郎。

translations.literal: Directors of Provisions, Medicine Storehouse, Inner Duty, and Palace Gate — all changed to Gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: The directors of provisions, the medicine storehouse, inner duty, and the palace gate were all retitled Gentlemen.

sentences.zh: 太子千牛為奉裕。

translations.literal: Heir Apparent Thousand-Ox became Offering Abundance.
translations.idiomatic: The heir's Thousand-Ox Guard was renamed Offering Abundance.

sentences.zh: 總章二年置司列、司戎少常伯各兩員。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zongzhang, two Junior Regular Preceptors each were established for Bureau of Rosters and Bureau of Arms.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zongzhang (669), two Junior Regular Preceptors each were added to the Bureaus of Rosters and Arms.

sentences.zh: 咸亨元年十二月詔：「龍朔二年新改尚書省百司及僕射已下官名，並依舊。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the first year of Xianheng, an edict: "The new changes of the second year of Longshuo to the hundred offices of the Department of State Affairs and names from Vice Directors downward — all follow the old.
translations.idiomatic: An edict of the twelfth month of the first year of Xianheng (670) declared: "The new Longshuo-era names for the Department of State Affairs and all offices from the vice directors downward shall all revert to the old designations.

sentences.zh: 其東宮十率府，有異上臺諸衛，各宜依舊為率府。

translations.literal: The Eastern Palace's ten commandant offices, which differed from the capital terrace guards, should each follow the old as commandant offices.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Palace's ten commandant offices, which had differed from the capital guard offices, shall each again be commandant offices as before.

sentences.zh: 其左司議郎除「左」字。

translations.literal: For Left Discussion Gentleman, remove the character "left."
translations.idiomatic: The word "left" shall be dropped from Left Discussion Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 其左、右金吾、左、右威衛，依新改」。

translations.literal: For Left and Right Golden Crow, Left and Right Majestic Guard — follow the new changes."
translations.idiomatic: The Left and Right Golden Crow and Left and Right Majestic Guards shall keep their new names."

sentences.zh: 永淳元年七月，置州別駕。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the first year of Yongchun, prefectural Vice Directors were established.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the first year of Yongchun (682), prefectural vice directors were established.

sentences.zh: 光宅元年九月，改尚書省為文昌台，左、右僕射為文昌左、右相。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the first year of Guangzai, Department of State Affairs was changed to Wenchang Terrace; Left and Right Vice Directors to Wenchang Left and Right Chancellors.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the first year of Guangzai (688), the Department of State Affairs became the Wenchang Terrace, and the left and right vice directors became the Wenchang Left and Right Chancellors.

sentences.zh: 吏部為天官，戶部為地官，禮部為春官，兵部為夏官，刑部為秋官，工部為冬官。

translations.literal: Ministry of Personnel became Heavenly Office; Household, Earthly Office; Rites, Spring Office; War, Summer Office; Punishments, Autumn Office; Works, Winter Office.
translations.idiomatic: Personnel became the Heavenly Office, Household the Earthly Office, Rites the Spring Office, War the Summer Office, Punishments the Autumn Office, and Works the Winter Office.

sentences.zh: 門下省為鸞台，中書省為鳳閣，侍中為納言，中書令為內史。

translations.literal: Chancellery became Phoenix Terrace; Secretariat, Phoenix Pavilion; Palace Attendant, Supplicator; Secretariat Director, Inner Scribe.
translations.idiomatic: The Chancellery became the Phoenix Terrace, the Secretariat the Phoenix Pavilion, the Palace Attendant the Supplicator, and the Secretariat Director the Inner Scribe.

sentences.zh: 太常為司禮，鴻臚為司賓，宗正為司屬，光祿為司膳，太府為司府，太僕為司僕，衛尉為司衛，大理為司刑。

translations.literal: Director of Ceremonies became Bureau of Rites; Director of Guests, Bureau of Guests; Director of the Imperial Clan, Bureau of Dependents; Director of Banquets, Bureau of Provisions; Director of the Treasury, Bureau of Treasury; Director of the Stud, Bureau of Servants; Director of the Guard, Bureau of Guard; Director of Justice, Bureau of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Ceremonies became Bureau of Rites, Guests Bureau of Guests, the Imperial Clan Bureau of Dependents, Banquets Bureau of Provisions, the Treasury Bureau of Treasury, the Stud Bureau of Servants, the Guard Bureau of Guard, and Justice Bureau of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 司農依舊。

translations.literal: Director of Agriculture followed the old.
translations.idiomatic: Agriculture kept its old name.

sentences.zh: 左、右驍衛為左右威衛，左、右武衛為左、右鷹揚衛，左、右威衛為左右豹衛，左、右領軍衛為左右玉鈴衛。

translations.literal: Left and Right Valiant Cavalry became Left and Right Majestic Guards; Left and Right Martial Guards, Left and Right Soaring Hawk Guards; Left and Right Majestic Guards, Left and Right Leopard Guards; Left and Right Army Inspector Guards, Left and Right Jade Bell Guards.
translations.idiomatic: The Left and Right Valiant Cavalry became Left and Right Majestic Guards; the Martial Guards became Soaring Hawk Guards; the former Majestic Guards became Leopard Guards; and the Army Inspector Guards became Jade Bell Guards.

sentences.zh: 左、右金吾衛依舊。

translations.literal: Left and Right Golden Crow Guards followed the old.
translations.idiomatic: The Left and Right Golden Crow Guards kept their old names.

sentences.zh: 御史台改為左肅政台，專知京百官及監諸軍旅，並承詔出使。

translations.literal: Censorate was changed to Left Rectification Terrace, exclusively overseeing capital officials and supervising all armies, and also undertaking missions by imperial edict.
translations.idiomatic: The Censorate became the Left Rectification Terrace, charged exclusively with oversight of capital officials and military forces and with carrying out missions by imperial edict.

sentences.zh: 更置右肅政台，專知諸州案察。

translations.literal: The Right Rectification Terrace was additionally established, exclusively overseeing investigation of all prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: A Right Rectification Terrace was also established, charged exclusively with investigating the prefectures.

sentences.zh: 垂拱元年二月，改黃門侍郎為鸞台侍郎，文昌都省為都台，主爵為司封，秘書省為麟台，內侍省為司宮台，少府監為尚方監。

translations.literal: In the second month of the first year of Chuigong, Yellow Gate Vice Minister was changed to Phoenix Terrace Vice Minister; Wenchang Chief Department to Chief Terrace; Fiefs to Bureau of Enfeoffments; Archive Secretariat to Unicorn Terrace; Palace Domestic Service to Palace Affairs Terrace; Palace Workshops Directorate to Imperial Works Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the first year of Chuigong (685), the Yellow Gate Vice Minister became Phoenix Terrace Vice Minister; the Wenchang Chief Department became the Chief Terrace; Fiefs became the Bureau of Enfeoffments; the Archive Secretariat became the Unicorn Terrace; the Palace Domestic Service became the Palace Affairs Terrace; and the Palace Workshops Directorate became the Imperial Works Directorate.

sentences.zh: 其左、右尚方兩署除「方」字。

translations.literal: For the Left and Right Imperial Works offices, the character "works" was removed.
translations.idiomatic: The Left and Right Imperial Works offices dropped the character for "works" from their titles.

sentences.zh: 將作監為營繕監，國子監為成均監，都水監為水衡監。

translations.literal: Works Directorate became Construction and Repair Directorate; Directorate of the Sons of the State, Academy of Equilibrium Directorate; Directorate of Waterways, Water Balance Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: The Works Directorate became Construction and Repair; the Directorate of the Sons of the State became the Academy of Equilibrium; and the Directorate of Waterways became the Water Balance Directorate.

sentences.zh: 其詹事府為宮尹府，詹事為太尹，少詹事為少尹。

translations.literal: The Household Administration became Palace Rectifier Office; Household Administrator, Grand Rectifier; Junior Household Administrator, Junior Rectifier.
translations.idiomatic: The Household Administration of the Heir Apparent became the Palace Rectifier Office; its administrator became Grand Rectifier and the junior administrator Junior Rectifier.

sentences.zh: 左、右內率府為左右奉裕率府，千牛為左右奉裕，左、右監門率府為左右控鶴禁率府，諸衛鎧曹改為胄曹，司膳寺肴藏署改為珍羞署。

translations.literal: Left and Right Inner Commandant Offices became Left and Right Offering Abundance Commandant Offices; Thousand-Ox, Left and Right Offering Abundance; Left and Right Gate Commandant Offices, Left and Right Crane-Control Forbidden Commandant Offices; armor bureaus of the guards changed to helmet bureaus; Provisions Directorate's dish storehouse changed to Delicacies Office.
translations.idiomatic: The Left and Right Inner Commandant Offices became Left and Right Offering Abundance Commandant Offices; the Thousand-Ox Guards became Left and Right Offering Abundance; the Gate Commandant Offices became Left and Right Crane-Control Forbidden Commandant Offices; guard armor bureaus were renamed helmet bureaus; and the Provisions Directorate's dish storehouse became the Delicacies Office.

sentences.zh: 十月，增置天官侍郎二員。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, two Heavenly Office Vice Ministers were added.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month, two vice ministers of the Heavenly Office were added.

sentences.zh: 又置左、右補闕、拾遣各二員。

translations.literal: Also established Left and Right Supplementation Omission and Left and Right Memorial Retrieval, two posts each.
translations.idiomatic: Left and Right Supplementation Omission and Left and Right Memorial Retrieval were also created, two posts on each side.

sentences.zh: 三年，加秋官侍郎一員。

translations.literal: In the third year, one Autumn Office Vice Minister was added.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, one vice minister of the Autumn Office was added.

sentences.zh: 永昌元年，置左、右司員外郎各一員。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongchang, one Left and one Right Bureau Extra Director were established.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongchang (689), one extra director each was added to the left and right bureaus.

sentences.zh: 天授二年，增置左、右補闕、拾遺各三員，通滿五員。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianshou, three more Left and Right Supplementation Omission and Memorial Retrieval posts each were added, reaching five in all.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianshou (691), three more posts each were added to the Left and Right Supplementation Omission and Memorial Retrieval offices, bringing each side to five incumbents in all.

sentences.zh: 長壽二年，增夏官侍郎三員。

translations.literal: In the second year of Changshou, three Summer Office Vice Ministers were added.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Changshou (693), three vice ministers of the Summer Office were added.

sentences.zh: 大足元年，加營繕少匠一員，左右羽林衛各增置將軍一員。

translations.literal: In the first year of Dazu, one Construction and Repair Junior Artisan was added; Left and Right Feathered Forest Guards each gained one general.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Dazu (701), one junior artisan was added to Construction and Repair, and each of the Left and Right Feathered Forest Guards gained an additional general.

sentences.zh: 洛、雍、並、荊、揚、益六州，置左、右司馬各一員。

translations.literal: For the six prefectures Luo, Yong, Bing, Jing, Yang, and Yi, one Left and one Right Administrative Aide each were established.
translations.idiomatic: For the six prefectures of Luo, Yong, Bing, Jing, Yang, and Yi, one left and one right administrative aide each were established.

sentences.zh: 長安三年，增置司勳員外郎一員，地官依舊置侍郎一員，洛、並及三大都督府司馬宜依舊置一員。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chang'an, one Bureau of Merit Extra Director was added; Earthly Office again had one Vice Minister; for Luo, Bing, and the three great area-command offices, one Administrative Aide each should again be established as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Chang'an (703), one extra director of the Bureau of Merit was added; the Earthly Office again had one vice minister; and Luo, Bing, and the three great area-command headquarters each again had one administrative aide as before.

sentences.zh: 神龍元年二月，台閣官名，並依永淳已前故事。

translations.literal: In the second month of the first year of Shenlong, terrace and pavilion office names all followed precedent before Yongchun.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the first year of Shenlong (705), the names of terrace and pavilion offices all reverted to the practice in force before Yongchun.

sentences.zh: 廢左、右司員外郎。

translations.literal: Left and Right Bureau Extra Directors were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The left and right bureau extra directors were abolished.

sentences.zh: 左右千牛衛各置大將軍一員。

translations.literal: Left and Right Thousand-Ox Guards each had one Grand General established.
translations.idiomatic: Each of the Left and Right Thousand-Ox Guards was given one grand general.

sentences.zh: 東都置太廟官吏，增置太常、大理少卿各一員。

translations.literal: At the Eastern Capital, ancestral temple officials were established; one Ceremonies and one Justice Vice Director each were added.
translations.idiomatic: Officials for the ancestral temple were established at the Eastern Capital, and one vice director each was added to Ceremonies and Justice.

sentences.zh: 二年，又置員外官凡二千餘人。

translations.literal: In the second year, extra-status officials numbering more than two thousand were also established.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, more than two thousand extra-status officials were also appointed.

sentences.zh: 超授閹官七品已上員外者，又千餘人。

translations.literal: Eunuchs promoted beyond grade to seventh rank and above as extra-status — also more than a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: More than a thousand eunuchs were also promoted beyond their proper grade to seventh rank and above as extra-status officials.

sentences.zh: 十二月，復置左右司員外郎各一員。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Left and Right Bureau Extra Directors were restored, one each.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, the left and right bureau extra directors were restored, one on each side.

sentences.zh: 景雲二年，復置太子左、右諭德、太子左、右贊善大夫各兩員。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jingyun, Heir Apparent Left and Right Moral Instructors and Heir Apparent Left and Right Assistant-in-Goodness Grand Masters were restored, two each.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jingyun (711), the heir's left and right moral instructors and left and right assistants-in-goodness were restored, two posts on each side.

sentences.zh: 雍、洛及大都督府長史加為三品階，別駕致敬，依前。

translations.literal: Chief aides of Yong, Luo, and great area-command offices were raised to third rank; vice directors' ceremonial salutations followed the former rule.
translations.idiomatic: The chief aides of Yong, Luo, and the great area-command headquarters were raised to the third rank, while vice directors' ceremonial salutations remained as before.

sentences.zh: 太極元年，光祿、大理、鴻臚、太府、衛尉、宗正，各增置少卿一員。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taiji, Banquets, Justice, Guests, Treasury, Guard, and Imperial Clan each had one Vice Director added.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Taiji (712), Banquets, Justice, Guests, the Treasury, the Guard, and the Imperial Clan each gained an additional vice director.

sentences.zh: 秘書少監、國子司業、少府少監、將作少匠、左右台中丞，各增置一員。

translations.literal: Archive Vice Director, National University Vice Rector, Palace Workshops Vice Director, Works Junior Artisan, and Left and Right Terrace Attendant Censors-in-Chief — one each added.
translations.idiomatic: One additional post each was created for the archive vice director, national university vice rector, palace workshops vice director, works junior artisan, and the left and right terrace attendant censors-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 雍、洛二州及益、並、荊、揚四大都督府，各增置司馬一員，分為左、右司馬。

translations.literal: For the two prefectures Yong and Luo and the four great area commands Yi, Bing, Jing, and Yang, one Administrative Aide each was added, divided into Left and Right Administrative Aides.
translations.idiomatic: For the two prefectures of Yong and Luo and the four great area commands of Yi, Bing, Jing, and Yang, one additional administrative aide was added on each side, divided into left and right aides.

sentences.zh: 開元元年十二月，改尚書左右僕射為左右丞相，中書省為紫微省，門下省為黃門省，侍中為監。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the first year of Kaiyuan, Left and Right Vice Directors of the Department of State Affairs became Left and Right Chancellors; Secretariat, Purple Forbidden Department; Chancellery, Yellow Gate Department; Palace Attendant, Supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the first year of Kaiyuan (713), the left and right vice directors became left and right chancellors; the Secretariat became the Purple Forbidden Department; the Chancellery became the Yellow Gate Department; and the Palace Attendant became Supervisor.

sentences.zh: 雍州為京兆府，洛州為河南府。

translations.literal: Yong Prefecture became Capital District Prefecture; Luo Prefecture, Henan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yong Prefecture became the Capital District Prefecture and Luo Prefecture the Henan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 長史為尹，司馬為少尹，錄事參軍為司錄參軍，余司改司為曹。

translations.literal: Chief Aide became Intendant; Administrative Aide, Junior Intendant; Recording Adjutant, Bureau Recording Adjutant; remaining offices changed "office" to "bureau."
translations.idiomatic: The chief aide became intendant, the administrative aide junior intendant, and the recording adjutant bureau recording adjutant; the remaining offices changed the word for "office" to "bureau."

sentences.zh: 五年九月，紫微省依舊為中書省，黃門省為門下省，黃門監為侍中。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the fifth year, Purple Forbidden Department again became Secretariat; Yellow Gate Department, Chancellery; Yellow Gate Supervisor, Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the fifth year (717), the Purple Forbidden Department again became the Secretariat, the Yellow Gate Department the Chancellery, and the Yellow Gate Supervisor the Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 二十四年九月，改主爵為司封。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the twenty-fourth year, Fiefs was changed to Bureau of Enfeoffments.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the twenty-fourth year (736), Fiefs was renamed the Bureau of Enfeoffments.

sentences.zh: 天寶元年二月，侍中改為左相，中書令改為右相，左、右丞相依舊為僕射，黃門侍郎為門下侍郎。

translations.literal: In the second month of the first year of Tianbao, Palace Attendant became Left Chancellor; Secretariat Director, Right Chancellor; Left and Right Assistants again Vice Directors; Yellow Gate Vice Minister, Chancellery Vice Minister.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the first year of Tianbao (742), the Palace Attendant became Left Chancellor and the Secretariat Director Right Chancellor; the left and right assistants again became vice directors; and the Yellow Gate Vice Minister became Chancellery Vice Minister.

sentences.zh: 改州為郡，刺史為太守。

translations.literal: Prefectures were changed to commanderies; regional inspectors, to grand administrators.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectures were renamed commanderies and regional inspectors grand administrators.

sentences.zh: 十一載正月，改吏部為文部，兵部為武部，刑部為憲部。

translations.literal: In the first month of the eleventh year, Ministry of Personnel became Literary Department; War, Martial Department; Punishments, Law Department.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the eleventh year (752), the Ministry of Personnel became the Literary Department, War the Martial Department, and Punishments the Law Department.

sentences.zh: 其行內諸司有部者並改。

translations.literal: Within the ministries, all offices bearing the character "department" were likewise changed.
translations.idiomatic: Within the ministries, all subordinate offices bearing the word for "department" were likewise renamed.

sentences.zh: 改駕部為司駕，改庫部為司庫，金部為司金，倉部為司儲，比部為司計，祠部為司禋，膳部為司膳，虞部為司虞，水部為司水。

translations.literal: Transport changed to Bureau of Carriages; Stores to Bureau of Stores; Coinage to Bureau of Coinage; Granaries to Bureau of Granaries; Audit to Bureau of Accounts; Sacrifices to Bureau of Sacrifices; Provisions to Bureau of Provisions; Forestry to Bureau of Parks; Waterways to Bureau of Water.
translations.idiomatic: Transport became the Bureau of Carriages, Stores the Bureau of Stores, Coinage the Bureau of Coinage, Granaries the Bureau of Granaries, Audit the Bureau of Accounts, Sacrifices the Bureau of Sacrifices, Provisions the Bureau of Provisions, Forestry the Bureau of Parks, and Waterways the Bureau of Water.

sentences.zh: 將作大匠為監，少匠為少監。

translations.literal: Works Chief Artisan became Director; Junior Artisan, Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: The works chief artisan became director and the junior artisan vice director.

sentences.zh: 至德二載十二月敕：「近日所改百司額及郡名並官名，一切依故事。」

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the second year of Zhide, an edict: "The recent changes to the designations of the hundred offices, commandery names, and office names — all follow precedent."
translations.idiomatic: An edict of the twelfth month of the second year of Zhide (757) declared: "The recent changes to the titles of the hundred offices, commandery names, and office names shall all revert to precedent."

sentences.zh: 於是侍中、中書令、兵、吏部等並仍舊。

translations.literal: Thereupon Palace Attendant, Secretariat Director, War, Personnel, and the rest all returned to the old.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the Palace Attendant, Secretariat Director, War, Personnel, and the rest all reverted to their former names.

sentences.zh: 罷郡為州，復以太守為刺史。

translations.literal: Commanderies were abolished in favor of prefectures; grand administrators again became regional inspectors.
translations.idiomatic: Commanderies were abolished in favor of prefectures, and grand administrators again became regional inspectors.

sentences.zh: 正第一品太師、太傅、太保、太尉、司徒、司空已上職事官、王爵。

translations.literal: Senior first rank Grand Preceptor, Grand Tutor, Grand Protector, Grand Commandant, Minister of Education, Minister of Works — the above are executive offices. King — a noble rank.
translations.idiomatic: Senior first rank Grand Preceptor, Grand Tutor, Grand Protector, Grand Commandant, Minister of Education, and Minister of Works — all executive offices. King — a noble rank.

sentences.zh: 《武德令》有天策上將，九年省。

translations.literal: The Wude Code had a Celestial-Strategy General-in-Chief; abolished in the ninth year.
translations.idiomatic: The Wude Code provided for a Celestial-Strategy General-in-Chief; the post was abolished in the ninth year.

sentences.zh: 從第一品開府儀同三司文散官。

translations.literal: Junior first rank Honored Companion with Ceremony Equal to the Three Dukes — civil honorary rank.
translations.idiomatic: Junior first rank Honored Companion with Ceremony Equal to the Three Dukes — a civil honorary rank.

sentences.zh: 開府儀同三司及特進不帶職事官者，朝參祿俸並同職事，仍隸吏部也、太子太師、太子太傅、太子太保已上職事官、驃騎大將軍武散官、嗣王、郡王、國公爵正第二品特進文散官、輔國大將軍武散官、開國郡公爵。

translations.literal: Honored Companions and Extraordinary Promoters who bore no executive office had court attendance and salary equal to executive officers, and were still subordinate to Personnel. Heir Apparent's Grand Preceptor, Grand Tutor, and Grand Protector — the above are executive offices. Swift-Cavalry Grand General — military honorary rank. Heir to a kingship, Commandery King, and State Duke — noble ranks. Senior second rank Extraordinary Promoter — civil honorary rank. Auxiliary-to-the-State Grand General — military honorary rank. Founding Commandery Duke — a noble rank.
translations.idiomatic: Honored Companions and Extraordinary Promoters without executive posts received court attendance and salary equal to executive officers and remained registered with Personnel. Heir Apparent's Grand Preceptor, Grand Tutor, and Grand Protector — all executive offices. Swift-Cavalry Grand General — a military honorary rank. Heir to a kingship, Commandery King, and State Duke — noble ranks. Senior second rank Extraordinary Promoter — a civil honorary rank. Auxiliary-to-the-State Grand General — a military honorary rank. Founding Commandery Duke — a noble rank.

sentences.zh: 《武德令》唯有公、侯、伯、子、男，貞觀十一年加開國之稱也、上柱國勳官。

translations.literal: The Wude Code had only Duke, Marquis, Earl, Viscount, and Baron; in the eleventh year of Zhenguan the designation "Founding" was added. Supreme Pillar of the State — merit rank.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Wude Code there were only Duke, Marquis, Earl, Viscount, and Baron; in the eleventh year of Zhenguan the epithet "Founding" was added. Supreme Pillar of the State — a merit rank.

sentences.zh: 《武德令》有尚書令，龍朔二年省。

translations.literal: The Wude Code had a Director of the Department of State Affairs; abolished in the second year of Longshuo.
translations.idiomatic: The Wude Code provided for a Director of the Department of State Affairs; the post was abolished in the second year of Longshuo.

sentences.zh: 自是正第二品無職事官。

translations.literal: From this time there was no executive office of senior second rank.
translations.idiomatic: From this point there was no executive office at senior second rank.

sentences.zh: 從第二品尚書左右僕射、太子少師、太子少傅、太子少保、京兆、河南、太原等七府牧、大都督揚、幽、潞、陝、靈、大都護單于、安西。

translations.literal: Junior second rank — Left and Right Vice Directors of the Department of State Affairs; Heir Apparent Junior Preceptor, Junior Tutor, and Junior Protector; prefects of the seven prefectures including the Capital District, Henan, and Taiyuan; Great Area Commanders of Yang, You, Lu, Shan, and Ling; and Great Protector-Generals of Chanyu and Anxi.
translations.idiomatic: Junior second rank — left and right vice directors of the Department of State Affairs; the heir's junior preceptor, junior tutor, and junior protector; the prefects of the seven great prefectures including the Capital District, Henan, and Taiyuan; the great area commanders of Yang, You, Lu, Shan, and Ling; and the great protector-generals of Chanyu and Anxi.

sentences.zh: 已上職事官、光祿大夫文散官、鎮軍大將軍武散官、開國縣公爵、柱國勳官正第三品侍中、中書令、吏部尚書舊班在左相上，《開元令》移在下、門下侍郎、中書侍郎舊班正四品上，大曆二年升、左右衛、左右驍衛、左右武衛、左右威衛、左右領軍衛、左右金吾衛、左右監門衛、左右羽林軍、左右龍武、左右英武六軍大將軍、左右千牛衛大將軍自左右衛已下，並為武職事官、戶部、禮部、兵部、刑部、工部尚書《武德令》，禮部次吏部，兵部次之，民部次之。

translations.literal: The above are executive offices. Grand Master for Splendid Happiness — civil honorary rank; Pacifier of the Army Grand General — military honorary rank. Founding County Duke — a noble rank. Pillar of the State — merit rank. Senior third rank Palace Attendant, Secretariat Director, Minister of Personnel — formerly ranked above the Left Chancellor; the Kaiyuan Code moved them below. Chancellery Vice Minister and Secretariat Vice Minister — formerly senior fourth rank, upper grade; raised in the second year of Dali. Left and Right Guards, Brave Guards, Martial Guards, Majestic Guards, Victorious Army Guards, Golden Crow Guards, Gate Guards, Forest of Feathers Army, Dragon Martial, Heroic Martial Six Armies grand generals, and Thousand-Ox grand generals — from the Left and Right Guards downward, all military executive offices. Ministers of the Household, Rites, War, Punishments, and Works — under the Wude Code, Rites followed Personnel, then War, then the People.
translations.idiomatic: All of the above are executive offices. Grand Master for Splendid Happiness — a civil honorary rank; Pacifier of the Army Grand General — a military honorary rank. Founding County Duke — a noble rank. Pillar of the State — a merit rank. Senior third rank Palace Attendant, Secretariat Director, and Minister of Personnel — formerly ranked above the Left Chancellor; under the Kaiyuan Code they were placed below. Chancellery Vice Minister and Secretariat Vice Minister — formerly senior fourth rank, upper grade; promoted in the second year of Dali. The grand generals of the Left and Right Guards, Brave Guards, Martial Guards, Majestic Guards, Victorious Army Guards, Golden Crow Guards, Gate Guards, Forest of Feathers Army, Dragon Martial, Heroic Martial Six Armies, and Thousand-Ox Guards — from the Left and Right Guards downward, all were military executive offices. Ministers of the Household, Rites, War, Punishments, and Works — under the Wude Code, Rites followed Personnel, then War, then the People.

sentences.zh: 貞觀年改以民部次禮部，兵部次之。

translations.literal: In the Zhenguan era it was changed so the People followed Rites, then War.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhenguan era the order was changed so the People followed Rites, then War.

sentences.zh: 則天初又改以戶部次吏部，禮部次之，兵部次之、太子賓客舊兼職，無品，《開元前令》定入官品也、太常卿、宗正卿天寶初升入正三品也、太子詹事、左右散騎常侍舊班從三品，廣德年升、內侍監唐初舊制，內侍省無三品官，內侍四員，秩四品。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zetian's reign it was again changed so the Household followed Personnel, then Rites, then War. Heir Apparent's Guest — formerly a concurrent post without rank; the pre-Kaiyuan code fixed it within the official grades. Director of Ceremonies and Director of the Imperial Clan — raised to senior third rank at the beginning of Tianbao. Household of the Heir Apparent and Left and Right Regular Attendants-in-Ordinary — formerly junior third rank; raised in the Guangde era. Palace Domestic Directorate — early Tang usage: the Palace Domestic Service had no third-rank post; four palace domestics, fourth rank.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Empress Wu's reign the order was changed again: Household after Personnel, then Rites, then War. Heir Apparent's Guest — formerly a concurrent post without formal rank; the pre-Kaiyuan code assigned it a place in the rank tables. Director of Ceremonies and Director of the Imperial Clan were raised to senior third rank at the beginning of the Tianbao era. Household of the Heir Apparent and the Left and Right Regular Attendants-in-Ordinary — formerly junior third rank; promoted in the Guangde era. Palace Domestic Directorate — under early Tang usage the Palace Domestic Service had no third-rank post; four palace domestics held fourth rank.

sentences.zh: 天寶十三年十二月，玄宗以中官高力士、袁思藝承恩遇，特置內侍監兩員，秩三品，以授之、中都督、上都護已上除八大將軍，並為文職事官、金紫光祿大夫文散官、冠軍大將軍武散官、懷化大將軍顯慶三年置，以授初附首領，仍隸諸衛也、上護軍勳官從第三品御史大夫舊班在秘書監九卿下，《開元令》移在上、秘書監、光祿、衛尉、太僕、大理、鴻臚、司農、太府卿、國子祭酒、殿中監、少府監、將作監、諸衛羽林〔入正三品〕千牛龍武將軍、下都督、上州刺史、京兆、河南、太原等七尹舊雍、洛長史從四品上，景雲二年加秩為從三品也、五大都督府長史舊從四品上，景雲二年加秩為從三品、大都護府副都護舊正四品上，《開元令》加入從三品、親王傅巳上並職事官。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the thirteenth year of Tianbao, because the eunuchs Gao Lishi and Yuan Siyi enjoyed imperial favor, Xuanzong specially established two Palace Domestic Directors of third rank and conferred them on the two men. Middle Protector, Superior Protector — apart from the eight great generals, the above are civil executive offices. Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon — civil honorary rank. Grand Champion General — military honorary rank. Grand General for Cherishing Transformation — established in the third year of Xianqing to confer on newly submitted tribal leaders; still subordinate to the various guards. Supreme Protector of the Army. Merit rank. Junior third rank Censor-in-Chief — formerly ranked below the Palace Secretariat and the Nine Directors; the Kaiyuan Code moved it above. Director of the Palace Secretariat; Directors of Imperial Entertainments, Guards, Imperial Stud, Judicial Review, Diplomatic Reception, Agriculture, Imperial Treasury; Chancellor of the National University; Directors of the Palace Directorate, Palace Workshops, and Construction; various guards and Forest of Feathers — entered senior third rank. Thousand-Ox and Dragon Martial generals; lower protector; superior-grade prefects; intendants of the seven prefectures including Capital, Henan, and Taiyuan — formerly chief administrators of Yong and Luo at junior fourth rank, upper grade; raised to junior third rank in the second year of Jingyun. Chief administrators of the five great protectorates — formerly junior fourth rank, upper grade; raised to junior third rank in the second year of Jingyun. Deputy Protector-General of the Great Protectorate — formerly senior fourth rank, upper grade; the Kaiyuan Code added it to junior third rank. Tutor to an Imperial Prince — the above are all executive offices.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the thirteenth year of Tianbao, because the eunuchs Gao Lishi and Yuan Siyi enjoyed the emperor's favor, Xuanzong specially created two third-rank Palace Domestic Director posts and conferred them on the two men. Middle Protector and Superior Protector — apart from the eight great generals, all of the above are civil executive offices. Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon — a civil honorary rank. Grand Champion General — a military honorary rank. Grand General for Cherishing Transformation — created in the third year of Xianqing to honor newly submitted tribal leaders; they remained attached to the various guard commands. Supreme Protector of the Army. A merit rank. Junior third rank Censor-in-Chief — formerly ranked below the Palace Secretariat and the Nine Directors; under the Kaiyuan Code it was placed above them. Director of the Palace Secretariat; directors of Imperial Entertainments, Guards, Imperial Stud, Judicial Review, Diplomatic Reception, Agriculture, and the Imperial Treasury; Chancellor of the National University; directors of the Palace Directorate, Palace Workshops, and Construction; and the various guards and Forest of Feathers Army — all entered senior third rank. Thousand-Ox and Dragon Martial generals; lower protector; superior-grade prefects; and intendants of the seven prefectures including the Capital, Henan, and Taiyuan — formerly chief administrators of Yong and Luo at junior fourth rank, upper grade; all raised to junior third rank in the second year of Jingyun. Chief administrators of the five great protectorates — formerly junior fourth rank, upper grade; raised to junior third rank in the second year of Jingyun. Deputy Protector-General of the Great Protectorate — formerly senior fourth rank, upper grade; the Kaiyuan Code placed it at junior third rank. Tutor to an Imperial Prince — all of the above are executive offices.

sentences.zh: 諸衛羽林、千牛龍武將軍為武，余並為文、銀青光祿大夫文散官、開國侯爵、雲麾將軍武散官、歸德將軍顯慶三年置，以授初附首領，仍隸諸衛也、護軍勳官。

translations.literal: The various guards, Forest of Feathers, Thousand-Ox, and Dragon Martial generals are military; the rest are civil. Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with Silver Seal and Blue Ribbon — civil honorary rank. Founding Marquis — noble rank. Cloud-Banner General — military honorary rank. General for Returning Virtue — established in the third year of Xianqing to confer on newly submitted tribal leaders; still subordinate to the various guards. Protector of the Army. Merit rank.
translations.idiomatic: The various guard commands, Forest of Feathers, Thousand-Ox, and Dragon Martial generals are military offices; the rest are civil. Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with Silver Seal and Blue Ribbon — a civil honorary rank. Founding Marquis — a noble rank. Cloud-Banner General — a military honorary rank. General for Returning Virtue — created in the third year of Xianqing to honor newly submitted tribal leaders; they remained attached to the various guard commands. Protector of the Army. A merit rank.

sentences.zh: 《武德令》有天策上將府長史、司馬，九年省也。

translations.literal: The Wude Code had Chief Administrator and Vice Administrator of the Celestial-Strategy General-in-Chief's Office; abolished in the ninth year.
translations.idiomatic: The Wude Code provided for a Chief Administrator and Vice Administrator of the Celestial-Strategy General-in-Chief's Office; both posts were abolished in the ninth year.

sentences.zh: 正第四品上階門下侍郎、中書侍郎舊正四品下階，《開元令》加入上階也、尚書左丞永昌元年進為正三品，如意元年復舊、吏部侍郎武德七年省諸司侍郎，吏部郎中為正四品上。

translations.literal: Senior fourth rank, upper grade — Chancellery Vice Minister and Secretariat Vice Minister: formerly senior fourth rank, lower grade; the Kaiyuan Code moved them to the upper grade. Left Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs: in the first year of Yongchang promoted to senior third rank; restored in the first year of Ruyi. Minister of Personnel: in the seventh year of Wude the various bureau vice ministers were abolished and the Personnel Bureau Director was senior fourth rank, upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: Senior fourth rank, upper grade — Chancellery Vice Minister and Secretariat Vice Minister were formerly senior fourth rank, lower grade; the Kaiyuan Code placed them in the upper grade. Left Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs was promoted to senior third rank in the first year of Yongchang (689) and restored in the first year of Ruyi (692). Minister of Personnel: in the seventh year of Wude (624) the various bureau vice ministers were abolished and the Personnel Bureau Director ranked senior fourth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 貞觀三年復置侍郎，其吏部郎中復舊為五品下、太常少卿、太子左庶子、太子少詹事、太子左右衛、左右司禦、左右清道、左右內率、左右監門率府率、中州刺史、軍器監武德初為正三品，七年省，八年復置，九年又省，十年復置北都軍器監、上都護府副都護、上府折沖都尉《武德令》統軍正四品下，後改為折沖都尉。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenguan the vice ministers were restored and the Personnel Bureau Director returned to fifth rank, lower grade — Vice Director of Ceremonies; Heir Apparent Left and Right Subprefects; Junior Household of the Heir Apparent; Heir Apparent Left and Right Guards; Left and Right Imperial Escort, Clear Way, Inner Rate, and Gate Rate commanders; prefect of a middle-grade prefecture; Armory Directorate: in early Wude senior third rank, abolished in the seventh year, restored in the eighth, abolished again in the ninth, restored in the tenth as Northern Capital Armory Directorate; Deputy Protector-General of the Superior Protectorate; Army-Suppressing Commandant of an upper-grade prefecture — under the Wude Code army commander was senior fourth rank, lower grade, later changed to army-suppressing commandant.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhenguan (629) the vice ministers were restored and the Personnel Bureau Director reverted to fifth rank, lower grade — Vice Director of Ceremonies; Heir Apparent Left and Right Subprefects; Junior Household of the Heir Apparent; Heir Apparent Left and Right Guards; Left and Right Imperial Escort, Clear Way, Inner Rate, and Gate Rate commanders; prefect of a middle-grade prefecture; and Armory Directorate: in early Wude senior third rank, abolished in the seventh year, restored in the eighth, abolished again in the ninth, and restored in the tenth as Northern Capital Armory Directorate; Deputy Protector-General of the Superior Protectorate; and Army-Suppressing Commandant of an upper-grade prefecture — under the Wude Code the army commander ranked senior fourth rank, lower grade, later redesignated army-suppressing commandant.

sentences.zh: 《垂拱令》始分為上中下府，改定官品。

translations.literal: The Chuigong Code first divided prefectures into upper, middle, and lower grades and revised official ranks.
translations.idiomatic: The Chuigong Code first divided prefectures into upper, middle, and lower grades and revised the official rank tables.

sentences.zh: 自此已上職事官。

translations.literal: From this point upward are executive offices.
translations.idiomatic: All of the above are executive offices.

sentences.zh: 率及折沖為武，余並為文也、正議大夫文散官也、開國伯爵、忠武將軍武散官、上輕車都尉勳官正第四品下階尚書右丞永昌元年進為從三品，如意元年復舊、諸司侍郎、太子右庶子、左右諭德、左右千牛衛、左右監門衛中郎將、親勳翊衛羽林中郎將、下州刺史《武德令》，中州刺史，正四品，下州刺史，從四品上。

translations.literal: Rate commanders and army-suppressing commandants are military; the rest are civil — Grand Master of Direct Counsel, civil honorary rank; Founding Earl, noble rank; Loyal Martial General, military honorary rank; Supreme Commandant of Light Chariots, merit rank. Senior fourth rank, lower grade — Right Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs: in the first year of Yongchang promoted to junior third rank; restored in the first year of Ruyi; vice ministers of the various bureaus; Heir Apparent Right Subprefect; Left and Right Moral Guides; Left and Right Thousand-Ox and Gate Guard Middle Commandants; Personal, Merit, and Assisting Guard Middle Commandants of the Forest of Feathers; prefect of a lower-grade prefecture — under the Wude Code the middle-grade prefect ranked senior fourth rank and the lower-grade prefect junior fourth rank, upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: Rate commanders and army-suppressing commandants are military offices; the rest are civil — Grand Master of Direct Counsel, a civil honorary rank; Founding Earl, a noble rank; Loyal Martial General, a military honorary rank; and Supreme Commandant of Light Chariots, a merit rank. Senior fourth rank, lower grade — Right Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs was promoted to junior third rank in the first year of Yongchang and restored in the first year of Ruyi; vice ministers of the various bureaus; Heir Apparent Right Subprefect; Left and Right Moral Guides; Left and Right Thousand-Ox and Gate Guard Middle Commandants; Personal, Merit, and Assisting Guard Middle Commandants of the Forest of Feathers; and prefect of a lower-grade prefecture — under the Wude Code a middle-grade prefect ranked senior fourth rank and a lower-grade prefect junior fourth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 《貞觀令》，一切為下州，加入正四品下。

translations.literal: The Zhenguan Code made all lower-grade prefectures and added them to senior fourth rank, lower grade.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhenguan Code treated all as lower-grade prefectures and placed them at senior fourth rank, lower grade.

sentences.zh: 自此已上職事官。

translations.literal: From this point upward are executive offices.
translations.idiomatic: All of the above are executive offices.

sentences.zh: 中郎將為武，余並為文也、通議大夫文散官、壯武將軍武散官從第四品上階秘書少監、八寺少卿、殿中少監、太子左右衛、司禦、清道、內率、監門副率、太子親勳翊衛中郎將、太子家令、太子率更令、太子僕、內侍、大都護親王府長史已上職事官。

translations.literal: Middle commandants are military; the rest are civil — Master of Free Counsel, civil honorary rank; Robust Martial General, military honorary rank.
